messages:
incident-bot: ALERT · kv-cache key cardinality and continuous-batching amplification detected on us-west-gpu-pool (models: qwen-mqa*, mistral-long*). Symptoms: rising kv_key_count, batch join spikes, sudden OOMs on worker-7, elevated 5xx for chat routes. Pager: zoe oncall. See https://ops.internal/alerts/1805012345

zoe (oncall): acked. quick triage: correlate 5xx with batch_inflight spikes. tagging sre and ml-infra. creating incident thread.

harry (sre): pulling logs. Saw repeated traces like: ```runtime: kv_cache_insert failed: out_of_memory (alloc 1.2GB)
route=chat-stream model=qwen-mqa-1 batch_join=18 seq=1024``` Also noticed autoscaler didn't relieve pressure because instances are pinned.

isabel (ml-infra): likely interaction of continuous-batching + high-kv-cardinality keys from GQA->MQA fallback behavior. Some sessions generate many small keys (per-turn prefixing) and continuous-batching groups them across users when sequence windows align. Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) disable continuous-batching at pool-level for models matching `*-mqa*` and `*-gqa*` 2) set per-model kv_shard_quota to 64k keys per-shard 3) apply soft-eviction policy: LRU-metric weighted by last-access and token-cost.

jack (eng-runtime): can stage these. I'll flip the flag for us-west only and push an emergency soft-evict that marks low-recently-used keys for eviction when mem > 70%. Doing a canary on gpu-pool-7.

karen (support): any customer-facing errors? I'll start scanning error reports and surface to affected accounts. If degraded, we'll notify.

harry (sre): applied pool-level feature flag at 05:04Z: `runtime.continuous_batching.disabled_for_mqa_gqa` scoped to us-west-gpu-pool. Also injected soft-evict policy. Monitoring dashboards updated.

incident-bot: ACTIONS TAKEN · flag toggled, soft-evict enabled, per-shard quotas staged. Runbook reference: https://runbooks.internal/kv-cache-continuous-batch-hotfix

zoe (oncall): metrics after change (t+6m): kv_key_count back to ~1.8x baseline from 15x, mem pressure falling, OOMs dropped to zero. p99 tail latency still slightly elevated on a handful of routes.

isabel (ml-infra): note — we observed model-specific patterns: qwen-mqa variants produced many micro-keys due to per-turn metadata; mistral-long had long KV lifetimes. Proposed short-term: reduce kv_ttl to 20s for new entries on affected models; medium-term: per-model batching profiles and key-normalization to collapse equivalent prefixes.

harry (sre): quick commands used: ```# snapshot pool stats curl -s "https://internal-api/pools/us-west-gpu-pool/stats" | jq '.kv.keys, .mem.percent, .batches.inflight'``` ```# toggle feature flag curl -XPOST https://internal-api/flags -d '{"name":"runtime.continuous_batching.disabled_for_mqa_gqa","value":true,"scope":"us-west-gpu-pool"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS'```

karen (support): support triage: 5 customer reports referencing intermittent 502/504 between 05:00-05:06Z, mostly apps on qwen-mqa in us-west. Sent proactive note to affected contacts: "We saw transient errors affecting qwen-mqa in us-west; mitigation applied. No data exposure. We'll follow up with timeline & postmortem."

lucas (pm): logging action items for postmortem: root cause analysis (cardinality + batching), customer impact quantification (tokens, requests, accounts), and remediation plan (per-model profiles, key normalization, alerting). Assign isabel+harry+jack.

jack (eng-runtime): added an emergency soft-evict PR for canary (link internal). Also added a guard: reject batch_joins > 12 for models with `mqa|gqa` tag; fallback to flow that preserves latency (smaller batches, increase concurrency).

zoe (oncall): status t+18m: mem pressure stabilized, kv keys ~1.02x baseline, error rate normalized, p99 within SLO for most routes. Keeping monitoring for 45m before demoting to followups.

harry (sre): note: one route experienced fallback amplification — when primary MQA instances were killed earlier, traffic hit a non-optimized fallback model causing higher token costs. We'll add alerting for cross-model fallback spikes.

isabel (ml-infra): follow-ups (tracked): 1) per-model batching profiles and whitelist for Llama endpoints that need continuous-batching 2) key-normalization library to reduce KV cardinality 3) add cardinality anomaly alert (kv_keys growth curve) 4) revisit default kv_ttl to shorter windows for high-cardinality models.

karen (support): customer impact summary: 5 customers affected, peak error rate ~0.04% of calls in window, majority recovered after mitigation, one customer requested postmortem. No data loss.

lucas (pm): schedule postmortem meeting and link to tracker: https://tracker.internal/INC-1805012345

zoe (oncall): handing off at 06:35Z to night team (harry_night). Current: mitigations in place, metrics stable, support notified, action items created. If anything spikes, page primary oncall.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED · mitigation stable for 50m. Close notes: temporary disables and soft-evictions restored cluster health; medium-term work required to prevent recurrence. Postmortem owners: isabel (ml-infra), harry (sre), jack (runtime).
